newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. warships in Gulf fire 17 missiles at Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warships in Gulf fire 17 missiles at Iraq.

text.p: United States Navy vessels in the Gulf fired 17 missiles early on Wednesday at Iraqi air defence targets in southern Iraq, a U.S. military spokesman said.
"A total of 17 cruise missiles were fired at selected Iraqi air defence targets in southern Iraq," said the spokesman of the second wave of missiles to be fired at Iraq in as many days.
The missiles were fired from two guided-missile destroyers, the USS Laboon and USS Russell, a submarine, the USS Jefferson City, and a destroyer, the USS Hewitt.
The United States had fired 27 cruise missiles at military targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday morning, saying Iraqi President Saddam Hussein had re-emerged as a threat to world security.

The purpose of the attacks is to "suppress Iraq's air defence capability" in the south as the United States and its Western allies widen a no-fly zone in southern Iraq on Wednesday to the 33rd parallel, closer to Baghdad, from the 32nd parallel, a U.S. officer said.

Wednesday's missile launches started shortly after 2:50 a.m. (2350 GMT Tuesday) in a "restrike of targets (attacked on Tuesday) to make sure we made the best job," the U.S. spokesman in the Gulf told Reuters.
